text:
claire: Noticed an uptick in "version pin TTL drift" alerts. Some tokens created during the v2 rollout are still pinned to v1 for ~10h even though we expected 5m TTL. Console shows odd histograms.

josh: Ugh. Thats the anchoring behavior we added to avoid flapping: if token had >=3 v1 successes historically we anchored TTL to long-tail. But I thought it only applied to pre-rollout tokens.

meena: Logs show two paths: (1) token metadata store had anchor=true (backfilled), (2) runtime refresh job skipped tokens that haven't called refresh endpoint. If a token never refreshes, TTL stays anchored.

vlad: Could be the backfill we ran in June that set anchor=true for accounts with legacy traffic. It used job id backfill-202406 and we didn't tag the anchor origin, so runtime treats them as organically anchored.

claire: Impact: quota dashboards show tenants as "stable v1" and hide v2 migration nudges. PMs are getting confused. Also reserved capacity may be underutilized.

josh: Two fixes: (A) mark backfilled anchors with origin=backfill and treat them as soft anchors (expire after 1h unless live affinity confirms), (B) add a runtime reconciliation sweep to clear anchors for tokens with a high v2 concordance in the last 30m.

meena: Telemetry gap: we don't currently emit the anchor origin in the routing trace, so console can't filter backfill-anchored tokens. We should add `anchor_origin` label and surface `version_pin_ttl_histogram` per-tenant.

vlad: Small ops risk: clearing anchors aggressively could cause brief migration blips. Suggest a staged approach: soft-unpin in canary tenants (pilot set of 50), monitor `route_affinity_mismatch_rate`, then widen.

claire: Agreed. Also QA found that when header `X-Client-Version` is missing, some edge proxies set a default of `1` internally. That defaulting creates false positives for anchors. We need edge to be explicit.

josh: I'll patch proxy to pass `X-Client-Version: unknown` if missing, rather than defaulting to 1. Cheap change.

meena: For reconciliation, I propose composite fingerprint dedupe to avoid double-counting where shadow/ingress duplicates exist. Use (tenant, token, path, request_hash) and keep a short LRU in the meter service. That will reduce billing noise.

vlad: Composite dedupe is OK but watch DB writes. Use streaming dedupe in the meter-ingest flow before writes. That avoids joins.

telemetry-bot: metric created: `route_affinity_mismatch_rate` (1m,1h) tagged by tenant, route_target, header_version. Sampling: 100% for pilot tenants for 48h.

ui-bot: console flag added: 'Prefer runtime affinity for banners' (off by default). Also added a new diagnostics card: 'Version pin ancestry' showing pin creation, origin, and age histogram.

claire: Action items: 1) ENG-32111 backfill-anchor-origin-tag + soft-anchor TTL (josh), 2) ENG-32112 proxy-default-version-explicit (josh), 3) TELE-7771 emit anchor_origin + pin_ttl_histogram (meena), 4) ENG-32113 meter-ingest composite dedupe streaming (vlad), 5) UI-4444 diagnostics card + pilot flag (product).

josh: Cutting a canary for proxy change and backfill tag patch: will target canary tenants group A (50 tenants).

vlad: We'll rate-limit reconciliation to 25 tenants/hour to avoid quota oscillation. Ops-runbook in ENG-32113 will include rollback criteria: >2% spike in 1m error rate or >5% change in average token latency for pinned tokens.

meena: I'll run a 24h baseline on `route_affinity_mismatch_rate` before soft-unpin so we can show delta. Also will export a CSV of affected tokens for billing to inspect.

claire: Thanks. If we see stable concordance improvements, PMs want a one-click console affordance to apply soft-unpin at tenant level. Leave that for later. Filing follow-ups per above.
